# Wikimedia Commons — ornamental alphabet plates (1898)

Eight ornamental alphabet plates from Lewis Foreman Day's *Alphabets Old
and New, for the Use of Craftsmen* (London: Batsford, 1898), a genuine
new creative category for the Studio library: hand-lettering/typography
design reference, distinct from every prior pack this session (which were
all illustration/decoration subject matter, not lettering). Directly in
scope per this session's mission — SweetOh Studio follows "the full range
of what people genuinely create and express," and hand-lettering is one
of the most commonly practiced creative crafts among POD/sticker/print
customers.

Eight stylistically distinct plates were chosen for real design variety
rather than volume: ornamental flourished capitals, hatched pattern-fill
capitals, a plain Roman serif alphabet with a construction grid, a Gothic
blackletter banner alphabet, bold white-on-black Roman capitals, ornate
illuminated initial letters in decorative frames, flourished script
capitals, and a geometric angular block alphabet.

## Rights and provenance

- Source: [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org), eight
  individual page-plate images from the "Internet Archive Book Images"
  Flickr Commons stream, each independently extracted from a scan of the
  1898 book (itself long out of copyright).
- License: "No restrictions" / "No known copyright restrictions" — a
  distinct Flickr Commons rights statement from the "Public domain" tag
  used elsewhere in this library, confirmed independently, live, for each
  file via the Wikimedia Commons API (`extmetadata.LicenseShortName ===
  "No restrictions"`, `extmetadata.UsageTerms === "No known copyright
  restrictions"`, `extmetadata.Restrictions === ""`).
  `node scripts/ingest-wikimedia-ornamental-alphabets.mjs` re-checks this,
  the exact page title, and the exact `descriptionurl` before generating
  Studio records; each original download is additionally verified against
  Wikimedia's own recorded SHA-1 hash for that upload. The raw API
  response for each file is preserved in `records/`.
- This Flickr stream is a large, semi-automated extraction of illustration
  crops from scanned book pages, and is known to sometimes contain messy
  or low-value crops (marginalia, blank space, running heads). Roughly 36
  plates from this book were available; each of the 8 selected here was
  visually inspected at full resolution before inclusion, and several
  candidates (including one initially miscategorized during triage) were
  swapped out or corrected after inspection rather than trusted on
  thumbnail alone.
- Images were downloaded from Wikimedia's original-resolution upload URLs
  (1312–2892px) and normalized to the Studio registry's 2400px ceiling.
  No cropping was needed.
- `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` records each asset's Commons URL, creator, date,
  and SHA-256 hashes of the original download and normalized output.
